title: Reflection in rank initial segments

based_on.title: Set Theory
based_on.pages: 80; 82–84 (§18, Theorem 18.16, limit-stage axioms only; §19, Theorem 19.1, Corollary 19.2 and its schema qualification); revision 2026-01-31

summary: Close stages under witnesses for a fixed finite family of formulas, obtain arbitrarily high reflecting levels, and construct countable transitive models of fixed finite axiom fragments.
abstract: A small rank stage can miss a witness to an existential statement even when all its parameters are present. Reflection shows how to choose stages that avoid this problem for any specified finite collection of formulas, simultaneously for every parameter tuple in the chosen stage. The construction repeatedly raises the height enough to include witnesses for parameters already available, then takes the union of the resulting sequence. Such heights occur above every ordinal and remain reflecting at increasing limit points. The argument works for any definable continuous increasing hierarchy of transitive sets. Applied to the cumulative hierarchy, it gives a rank model of each fixed finite collection of ZFC axioms. A countable elementary substructure and the Mostowski collapse then give a countable transitive model of that same finite collection. The finite collection remains fixed throughout these assertions.
